quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results deck: EBITDA NT$6,969 million (EBITDA margin 45.8%, vs 29.0% in Q1 2026), capex NT$2,202 million (Q1 2026: NT$3,460 million; Q2 2025: NT$7,537 million) and depreciation NT$2,408 million; 1H26 capex NT$5,662 million vs NT$19,094 million in 1H25. The company notes Q2 gross margin remained broadly stable QoQ despite revenue growth, mainly reflecting higher depreciation, compensation accruals and cost pressures from freight and energy; Q2 profit before tax, net profit and EPS rose QoQ mainly from mark-to-market gains on Siltronic shares; and Q2 inventories rose QoQ mainly due to inventory build-up in preparation for anticipated demand in H2. Simulated 1H26 figures that exclude the impacts of the major expansions in the U.S., Italy and Japan and the Siltronic mark-to-market changes: gross margin 32.4% (reported 20.7%), operating margin 22.6% (reported 9.9%), EPS NT$11.26 (reported NT$11.87). Prepayment balance shown on the deck: NT$20.8 billion (US$0.66 billion), including guarantee.

quarterly_data.signal: Company executive comments (Q2 2026 deck): an improved outlook as AI demand broadens while the recovery remains gradual and uneven - customer inventories are returning to healthier levels and order visibility is improving across a wider range of end markets, with AI demand extending beyond advanced nodes to selected mature nodes such as industrial and power. Customers are placing greater emphasis on supply certainty, regional production and resilience. The company says technology roadmaps are tightening advanced wafer supply: AI, new packaging technologies and advanced process migration raise wafer intensity and qualification requirements, and supply-demand conditions remain tight across selected high-specification products, supported by strong demand and a limited number of suppliers capable of producing qualified advanced wafers. On memory it says that despite ongoing capacity expansion, supply constraints are expected to persist over the next few years, customers are securing supply through long-term agreements, and rising HBM adoption is driving greater wafer requirements; agentic AI is broadening data-center architectures to include greater CPU content; and packaging technologies including CoWoS, CoPoS, wafer-on-wafer and HBM stacking require multiple wafer layers and tighter specifications, increasing wafer requirements per system.

Product and site status (Q2 2026 deck): 12-inch SOI - driven by continued growth in silicon photonics demand, SOI production continues to ramp up, with demand exceeding supply; GaN - capacity remains fully utilized with expansion progressing (~30% completed, ~20% underway); SiC - 12-inch SiC qualification is progressing with multiple customers, supporting future commercialization; square wafers - qualification activities with multiple customers are progressing smoothly. At the St. Peters, Missouri (U.S.) site customer sampling is ongoing and RF-SOI and silicon photonics products have entered small-volume production. The company says the focus of its expansion investments is shifting from fab construction to customer qualification and production ramp-up as new capacity begins contributing to revenue and earnings.
quarterly_data.figure: 12-inch SOI demand exceeding supply; GaN expansion ~30% completed, ~20% underway
